content: These references include research articles, review articles, abstracts, posters, and editorials, covering various diagnostic methods, their sensitivity, specificity, and clinical applications. Many studies compare HCV core antigen assays with nucleic acid testing (NAT) or other serological methods, highlighting their potential utility in diagnosing acute and chronic HCV infections, monitoring treatment, and screening blood donations. Some references also discuss the development of novel assays, their performance in specific populations (e.g., dialysis patients, HIV co-infected individuals), and their cost-effectiveness in resource-limited settings. Additionally, the list includes meta-analyses, evaluations of assay performance during the seroconversion window period, and discussions on the clinical significance of HCV markers in different liver diseases.
